candidate.blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: monitor for adverse medication reactions, safely administer parenteral medications, interpret medication-related laboratory findings, and intervene for complications.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — safety monitoring after intravenous iron sucrose
candidate.educational_objective: After intravenous iron sucrose, monitor for hypersensitivity and hypotension and observe the client for the labeled post-infusion period rather than assuming immediate discharge is safe.

options.A: Observe for signs of hypersensitivity for at least 30 minutes and until the client is clinically stable, while also monitoring for hypotension.
options.B: Discharge the client immediately because clinically important reactions do not occur after iron sucrose administration ends.
options.C: Monitor only for hypoglycemia because hypersensitivity and hypotension are not recognized risks of intravenous iron sucrose.
options.D: Obtain a serum iron level immediately after the infusion because this is the preferred time to assess iron status.

candidate.rationale: Current FDA labeling for iron sucrose requires observation for signs and symptoms of hypersensitivity during and after administration for at least 30 minutes and until the client is clinically stable; personnel and therapies for treatment of serious hypersensitivity reactions must be immediately available. The label also warns that clinically significant hypotension can occur and should be monitored during and after administration. In addition, serum iron testing should not be performed for at least 48 hours after intravenous dosing because transferrin saturation rises rapidly. Therefore, A is correct. B and C ignore labeled safety risks, and D uses an explicitly inappropriate timing for serum iron measurement.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Directly supports the exact post-infusion hypersensitivity-observation period, hypotension monitoring, and avoidance of immediate post-dose serum iron testing.
candidate.source_document_title: IRON SUCROSE injection — Official Prescribing Information
candidate.source_locator: Section 5.1, Hypersensitivity Reactions: monitor during and after administration for at least 30 minutes and until clinically stable; serious-reaction personnel/therapies must be immediately available. Section 5.2, Hypotension: monitor for signs/symptoms during and following each administration. Section 5.3, Iron Overload: TSAT rises rapidly; do not perform serum iron measurements for at least 48 hours after IV dosing.
